intro: Preschool teachers instruct, coordinate and care for young children, skills that transfer to tutoring, therapy and adult education. The closest of the 25 careers below is Childcare Workers at an 87% match, but Self-Enrichment Teachers are 83% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $46,800, or 23% more.
why_it_works: A preschool day means teaching through play, managing a busy room and keeping parents informed. O*NET rates instructing at 4 out of 5 for this job, and coordination and social perceptiveness at 3.75. Tutoring, therapy assistant and adult education roles use those strengths. Many matches pay more than the $38,140 preschool median. The skills to build include time management and technology.
tips: Occupational Therapy Assistants earn $72,300, which is 90% more, after an associate program.
Tutoring is an easy test: tutors earn $43,350, or 14% more, often with flexible hours.
Keep samples of lesson plans and progress notes for teaching and aide applications.

faq.q: What jobs can former preschool teachers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Childcare Workers (87%), Self-Enrichment Teachers (83%) and Tutors (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Adult education and ESL instructors are 78% matched and earn $61,540, which is 61% more than the $38,140 preschool median, though they usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Which careers for preschool teachers pay more?
faq.a: 18 of the 25 matches pay more. Occupational Therapy Assistants earn $72,300 (90% more), Physical Therapist Assistants $68,380 (79% more) and licensed practical nurses $64,400 (69% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All need a license or program.

faq.q: Do preschool teachers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Sometimes. 16 of the 25 matches need no more education than preschool teachers already have, including 7 of the top 10. In the closest match, 39% of workers have a high school diploma as their highest level, so childcare and tutoring roles are easy first steps.

faq.q: What skills should preschool teachers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, programming, technology design and time management. Service orientation already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so health or technical training is the main step toward better pay.
